label: Founded by God immediately: In the strong rival gloss, God's own constitutive act establishes the…
definition: In the strong rival gloss, God's own constitutive act establishes the society without an envoy or creature supplying that constitutive act. An envoy's authorization alone does not make the act God's own. This stronger exclusion is not entailed merely by calibrating FoundedAsTeachingAuthority to a direct-founding relation. In the encoded Jesus-specific comparison, STMT-DIVINE-FOUNDING-IS-EXCLUSIVE-IMMEDIATE adds an explicit exclusion for commissioned Jesus events; the full exclusion of all possible creatures is not encoded.
note: Rival sense recorded so that the envoy-founding premise cannot pass silently between senses. No corpus statement uses it as its reading of FoundedAsTeachingAuthority; a source defending it (for example an ecclesiology for which only an invisible church is God's own work) would make it a sourced rival. Minimal direct calibration, Jesus-specific exclusion, and a nonempty commissioned-event witness are separate propositions. The old universal claim that an immediate-only reading makes the envoy bridge false was too strong: compatibility can hold, and without events the bridge is vacuous. No identity or distinctness of Jesus and a God candidate is inferred.
